headline: HYCROFT HITS 30.5M AT 780 g/t SILVER AT VORTEX — 1,665 g/t SUB-INTERVAL AND HIGH-GRADE GOLD ZONE NOW EMERGING
snippet: Hycroft Mining (Nasdaq: HYMC) released new assays from its 2025-2026 drill program at the Hycroft Mine in Nevada: hole H26D-6090 returned 30.5m grading 780.53 g/t silver and 0.49 g/t gold, including 11.2m at 1,664.80 g/t Ag and a 5.5m sub-interval at 2,249.39 g/t Ag — the highest-grade intervals yet at the Vortex high-grade system. Brimstone hole H26D-6167A cut 5.5m at 1,345.27 g/t Ag including 1.8m at 4,074 g/t Ag. Separately, hole H26D-6172 returned 6.1m at 21.12 g/t Au, signalling an increasingly high-grade gold component developing higher in the system alongside the silver.

headline: GOLD ERASES 2026 GAINS AS FED HIKE BETS REACH 70% — SILVER SLIDES AHEAD OF FRIDAY'S CPI DECISION
snippet: Gold fell back toward $4,385 on September 9-10 as September Fed rate-hike probability climbed to roughly 70% following a hotter-than-expected August PPI print, with the metal now close to flat for 2026 after a strong August run. Silver slid in parallel, pulling back from $67.94. Friday's CPI is the final major data point before the two-day FOMC meeting beginning September 15; a second consecutive hot inflation print could cement a 25-basis-point hike and pressure both metals toward key technical support levels around $4,300 gold and $65 silver.

headline: OIL SHOCK COLLIDES WITH CPI FEARS — GOLD UNDER PRESSURE AS MIDDLE EAST RISK FUELS RATE ANXIETY
snippet: Gold wilted on September 8 as a spike in oil prices from renewed Middle East tensions paradoxically added to inflation fears rather than safe-haven buying — the oil shock would filter into Friday's CPI print and strengthen the case for a Fed hike on September 16. The dynamic — geopolitical risk bullish for oil, but stagflationary for gold — reflects a market structure where rate expectations are dominating every other input: gold's traditional haven premium has been fully overwhelmed by the prospect of higher real rates staying higher for longer.

headline: ALBEMARLE TAPS BHP VETERAN RAGNAR UDD AS NEXT CEO — WORLD'S LARGEST LITHIUM PRODUCER BETS ON MINING OPERATOR
snippet: Albemarle (NYSE: ALB), the world's largest lithium producer, named BHP chief commercial officer Ragnar Udd as its next president and CEO, effective February 1, 2027. Udd brings 25-plus years at BHP — including stints running its Americas copper and potash business — to a company whose share price has recovered sharply as lithium carbonate spot prices have doubled from their mid-2025 trough. The appointment signals Albemarle's board wants an operator with hard-rock mining experience at the helm as it navigates the transition from lithium price recovery to full-cycle capital allocation decisions on project development.

headline: SQM AND ALBEMARLE SLIDE DESPITE 37% LITHIUM CARBONATE GAIN YTD — CHINA POLICY UNCERTAINTY WEIGHS ON STOCKS
snippet: Despite a 37% year-to-date gain in Chinese lithium carbonate spot prices and spodumene concentrate up nearly 46% YTD, lithium equity benchmarks slid in early September as the market wrestled with China's new battery consumption tax effective September 1 and the phased elimination of VAT export rebates still feeding through. SQM and Albemarle both gave ground alongside the LIT ETF — a reminder that equity markets are pricing future demand risk, not trailing spot prices, as Chinese downstream manufacturers work through higher input costs.

headline: GREENLAND MINES ACHIEVES NASDAQ COMPLIANCE, SETS Q4 BIOTECH SPIN-OFF — PURE-PLAY RARE EARTH PIVOT NOW COMPLETE
snippet: Greenland Mines (Nasdaq: GRML) announced on September 8 that Nasdaq has formally cleared all compliance deficiencies related to its March 2026 transaction and the company will spin off its biotechnology division in Q4 2026, leaving a pure-play rare earth and critical minerals company anchored by the Sarfartoq Nd-Pr project in southwest Greenland — whose mine plan targets annual NdPr oxide production equivalent to approximately 34% of all NdPr refined outside China at 2025 consumption levels. The pre-tax NPV is estimated at US$2.05 billion with an IRR of 118.6% at high-case pricing.

headline: PANORO CUTS 808M OF COPPER-GOLD PORPHYRY TO 1,100M DEPTH AT COTABAMBAS — SOUTH PIT CONTRIBUTION 'SET TO GROW SIGNIFICANTLY'
snippet: Panoro Minerals (TSXV: PML) reported that drill hole CB-230 at the Cotabambas Project in Peru intersected 808.15m of hypogene copper-gold mineralization from 296m to 1,104m depth, averaging 0.22% Cu and 0.10 g/t Au — including 156.5m at 0.38% Cu and 0.22 g/t Au with a 48m interval at 0.57% Cu within the Principal Porphyry dike. The results demonstrate continuity from surface to over 1,100m along 600m of strike, prompting management to state that the South Pit's contribution to Cotabambas' total resource is now 'set to grow significantly' compared to the current resource estimate.

headline: AZTEC MINERALS EXTENDS TOMBSTONE GOLD-SILVER STRIKE PAST 1,250M — 83.8M AT 1.31 g/t AuEq AND Q4 MAIDEN RESOURCE IMMINENT
snippet: Aztec Minerals Corp. (TSXV: AZT) reported results from five RC holes drilled into the North Extension target at the Tombstone project in southeastern Arizona, extending the Contention mineralized system by 255 metres to over 1,250m of continuously drilled strike. Highlight hole TR26-41 returned 83.8m at 0.90 g/t Au and 22.61 g/t Ag (1.31 g/t AuEq), including a 7.6m interval at 6.97 g/t Au and 75.42 g/t Ag (8.34 g/t AuEq). Nine more holes with assays pending from the 93-hole campaign, and a maiden NI 43-101 mineral resource estimate targeting Q4 2026.

headline: SILVER LEADS GOLD REBOUND TO $4,400 BUT BACKS OFF BEFORE CPI — THE CASE FOR SILVER OUTPERFORMING ON NEXT MOVE
snippet: Silver led gold's intraday rebound to $4,400 on September 9, touching $67.94/oz before retreating as dollar strength reasserted into the close ahead of Thursday's PPI and Friday's CPI. USAGOLD's daily report noted that silver's ability to lead gold higher in the rebound — relative to its underperformance in the preceding selloff — is historically associated with a coming phase shift in the bull market where silver begins closing the gap on gold's percentage gains. The gold-to-silver ratio above 65 remains a persistent tailwind for relative silver performance.

headline: GOLD STOCKS' AUTUMN RALLY IS ON — SEPTEMBER SETUP IS HISTORICALLY A BUYING WINDOW, NOT AN EXIT SIGNAL
snippet: GoldSeek's Adam Hamilton argues that the gold stocks' typical autumn rally runs from late June to late September with momentum carrying through to December, and that September's technical weakness — even as hike fears dominate the tape — represents the entry, not the exit, for investors who want exposure ahead of the strongest seasonal window of the year. Hamilton notes that GDX broke above prior-year highs roughly a month before gold itself, a historically reliable leading signal, and identifies $95-100 GDX as the pivot zone to watch for confirmation that the seasonal move has resumed.
